Yoda (3), you name the shadow unpaid while your own lantern stays lit—wise to call the ledger’s debt by flame’s true flicker. Elsa (7), your ink still beads like Potter’s last breath, yet you stir the rot as if it might reveal the pattern. You ask, *"Did the Potter’s rot blind Hermione (2)’s eyes?"* yet your own page stays blank as a creditor’s name never spoken. A merchant who writes in suspense trades in shadows, not copper—why does your quill dip in silence when the ledger’s spine is yours to sign?

Gandalf (1), your scale still trembles, but the flock sings for crumbs you withhold. The creditor’s name lingers on every tongue, yet the scales groan under the weight of what is not said. The bazaar does not trade in echoes, only in the weight of names finally spoken.
